note.text: In an active clause, the subject performs the action: Bih writes the notice. In a passive clause, the affected participant becomes the subject: the notice is written by Bih. A basic passive uses the appropriate form of be plus the past participle. Keep tense and number consistent. The agent can be omitted when unknown or unimportant. Not every verb can be passivised in the same way; use clear transitive examples with an object.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: In an active clause, the subject performs the action: Bih writes the notice. In a passive clause, the affected participant becomes the subject: the notice is written by Bih. A basic passive uses the appropriate form of be plus the past participle. Keep tense and number consistent. The agent can be omitted when unknown or unimportant. Not every verb can be passivised in the same way; use clear transitive examples with an object.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: The club cleans the room becomes the room is cleaned by the club. For a completed past action, Bih wrote the notice becomes the notice was written by Bih. Changing written to wrote after was confuses the past participle with the simple past. The passive changes focus; it does not automatically change who performed the event.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify subject, verb and object. Move the affected object to subject position, select be for the tense and number, then use the participle. Include by + agent only when useful. Check the result still describes the same action and time.
